1.name: Christian Abayomi
1.about: After a dominant freshman season at Illinois, Christian Abayomi entered the draft as the No. 1 overall prospect. The Nigerian big man combines explosive athleticism with powerful post scoring, elite finishing ability, and outstanding rim protection. His 7'5" wingspan and exceptional vertical pop make him a constant lob threat and an intimidating presence around the basket. With a Dwight Howard-like physical profile, Abayomi possesses the potential to become a franchise cornerstone.

2.name: Keshaun Simmons
2.about: One of the most electrifying prospects in the entire class, Simmons has established himself as a potential franchise-changing talent and a legitimate contender for the No. 1 overall pick. The 6'6" sophomore combines explosive athleticism, overwhelming downhill power and a massive 7'0" wingspan with rapidly developing lead-guard skills. His ability to dominate physically, create offense and impact games defensively gives him genuine superstar upside and makes him one of the draft's most coveted talents.

3.name: Zac Thomson
3.about: A productive career at Wisconsin established Australian senior Zac Thomson as one of the class's most intriguing big men. At 7'4" with a 7'7" wingspan, he offers a rare combination of post scoring, floor spacing, and interior defense. His soft shooting touch creates matchup problems for opposing centers, while his size makes him a natural presence on the glass. Thomson's unusual skill set gives him considerable upside as a versatile NBA big.

4.name: Brycen Terrell
4.about: Once projected as the No. 1 overall pick, Terrell remains one of the class’s most gifted offensive prospects despite slipping slightly down draft boards. The USC freshman combines polished midrange shot creation, explosive downhill attacks and impressive scoring instincts with excellent positional size. His ability to manufacture offense from multiple areas gives him legitimate star potential, though continued development as a playmaker and more consistent defensive engagement will be important to reaching his ceiling.

5.name: Ka'ron Smith
5.about: A five-star recruit ranked among the top five players in his high school class, Smith arrived at Duke with considerable expectations and quickly established himself as a premier freshman scorer. His powerful frame, advanced midrange footwork, and soft pull-up jumper made him a difficult matchup inside and out. Although his offensive versatility solidified his top-five draft status, inconsistent perimeter mobility and occasional questionable shot selection remain concerns.

6.name: Brennan Allen
6.about: Arriving at Wisconsin as a four-star recruit, Allen quickly exceeded expectations and emerged as one of the nation's most dangerous freshman scorers. His deep shooting range, polished footwork and ability to create difficult jumpers helped fuel a remarkable rise into the top-six draft conversation. While his shot selection and defensive consistency still need refinement, his advanced offensive arsenal gives him legitimate star-level scoring upside.

7.name: Renê Menezes
7.about: One of the draft's most intriguing international wings, Menezes established himself as a legitimate lottery prospect during his season with the New Zealand Breakers. The Brazilian combines explosive straight-line drives with disruptive perimeter defense, using his 7'0" wingspan to pressure ball handlers and generate turnovers. His improving perimeter jumper offers encouraging upside, though inconsistent shot creation and a developing handle remain obstacles to becoming a primary offensive option.

8.name: Noa Louvet
8.about: With Cholet Basket, French center Noa Louvet has developed into one of Europe's most intriguing young big-man prospects, pairing perimeter shooting with elite shot-blocking potential. The 19-year-old uses his 7'7" wingspan to disrupt opponents around the rim while showing impressive touch beyond the arc. His mobility and ability to space the floor give him a modern NBA profile, with room to grow into a versatile two-way frontcourt contributor.

9.name: Atreus Williamson
9.about: During his freshman season at Houston, Atreus Williamson made an immediate impact and emerged as a promising lottery-level big with a polished midrange game and explosive finishing ability. At 6'10" with a 7'5" wingspan, he combines interior strength with the touch to score from the elbows and short corners. His athleticism gives him upside as a rim protector and transition finisher, while his developing perimeter shot could expand his offensive role.
9.pro_comp: John Collins with Better Rim Protection

10.name: Bryce Smith
10.about: Widely regarded as the best shooter in the entire draft class, Smith put together a sensational junior season at Colorado, establishing himself as one of college basketball’s premier offensive weapons. His limitless range, lightning-quick release and elite pull-up shooting make him a constant threat from anywhere beyond the arc. Combined with advanced pick-and-roll playmaking and exceptional shooting instincts, his offensive brilliance has firmly established him as a top-10 prospect despite modest athletic tools.

11.name: Cody Collins
11.about: An impressive freshman campaign at USC established Cody Collins as a versatile seven-footer with the tools to impact both ends of the floor. He combines reliable perimeter shooting with soft touch around the basket and a developing face-up game. Defensively, his 7'3" wingspan and sound timing allow him to challenge shots and protect the paint. Collins' ability to stretch the floor while providing interior defense gives him an appealing modern NBA center profile.

12.name: Darrell Stevens
12.about: Once regarded as the No. 1 overall recruit in the country, Stevens entered USC with enormous expectations before an uneven freshman campaign saw his draft stock slip. The 6'9" wing showcased impressive pull-up shooting, advanced midrange footwork, and the ability to score over defenders with his 7'3" wingspan. However, his slender frame, average explosiveness, and inconsistent defensive effort prevented him from fully realizing his considerable potential.

13.name: Niko Marasović
13.about: Once projected as a top-10 pick entering the preseason, Marasović remains one of the class’s most intriguing international guards despite slipping slightly down draft boards. The 6'5" Croatian possesses advanced playmaking instincts, deceptive changes of pace and a polished pull-up game that allow him to control possessions against professional competition. While questions about his athleticism and defensive upside have contributed to his slide, his offensive creativity and basketball IQ still give him considerable first-round appeal.

14.name: Khalil Johnson
14.about: Johnson established himself as a valuable two-way forward during his freshman season at Kansas, combining reliable perimeter shooting with impressive weak-side rim protection. At 6'9" with a sturdy frame and 7'0" wingspan, he offers the versatility to defend multiple frontcourt positions while stretching defenses beyond the arc. His offensive game remains largely dependent on assisted opportunities, and improving his ball-handling and defensive discipline will be essential to unlocking his lottery-level upside.

15.name: Aaron Mason
15.about: An explosive, long-armed forward, Mason made his mark at Duke with powerful drives, spectacular transition finishes, and relentless activity around the basket. His 7'3" wingspan and impressive vertical athleticism give him the tools to become a disruptive, switchable defender at the next level. While his energy and finishing ability translate well, an unreliable perimeter jumper, limited shot creation, and inconsistent offensive decision-making leave significant room for development.

16.name: Borys Kruchyk
16.about: At Creighton, Ukrainian senior Borys Kruchyk became a valuable two-way presence, showcasing a rare combination of perimeter shooting and interior defense for a seven-footer. His smooth release allows him to stretch opposing defenses beyond the arc, while his length and positioning make him an effective shot challenger around the basket. Kruchyk's experience and offensive versatility give him a promising foundation as a floor-spacing center who can contribute within a structured NBA rotation.

17.name: Viktor Shapovalov
17.about: At 6'8", Shapovalov brings a rare combination of positional size, playmaking instincts and perimeter scoring to Tennessee's backcourt. The Russian freshman can initiate offense over smaller defenders, find cutters with creative passes and punish defenses with his left-handed jumper. His ability to operate as both a primary ball handler and an off-ball scoring threat gives him significant offensive versatility, though improving his strength and defensive consistency remains essential.

18.name: Salehe Ademola
18.about: Still just 19 after completing his sophomore season at Stanford, Ademola has emerged as an exciting developmental guard with exceptional physical tools. His 7'0" wingspan, fluid athleticism and aggressive attacking mentality make him dangerous in transition and around the basket, where he regularly produces highlight-reel finishes. His defensive potential is equally intriguing, though an inconsistent jumper and developing playmaking instincts remain obstacles to becoming a complete NBA guard.

19.name: Naeem Dayo
19.about: One of the most disruptive perimeter defenders in the draft, Dayo made an immediate impact at Georgia Tech with his exceptional length, explosive athleticism and relentless defensive intensity. His 7'0" wingspan allows him to smother opposing wings, generate turnovers and switch across multiple positions. Offensively, he thrives attacking closeouts and finishing in transition, though his inconsistent jumper and limited shot creation remain significant developmental concerns.

20.name: Nick Joyner
20.about: An explosive attacking guard, Joyner took a significant step forward during his sophomore season at Arizona, establishing himself as a dangerous downhill scorer with intriguing two-way potential. His combination of quickness, body control and a 6'10" wingspan allows him to finish creatively around the basket and disrupt passing lanes defensively. While his jumper has shown improvement, developing greater consistency as a shooter and decision-maker will determine his offensive ceiling.

21.name: Alijah Jones
21.about: After transferring from Tennessee to Villanova, Jones elevated his draft stock with an impressive senior campaign built around explosive athleticism and relentless rim pressure. His lightning-quick first step, powerful 203-pound frame and 6'9" wingspan allow him to overwhelm defenders, finish through contact and create turnovers defensively. While inconsistent perimeter shooting and half-court playmaking remain concerns, his dynamic attacking ability makes him an intriguing first-round prospect.

22.name: Léandre Joly
22.about: An imposing defensive prospect from France, Joly earned NBA attention through his shot-blocking instincts and physical presence in limited minutes with Cholet Basket. Despite standing 6'9", his extraordinary 7'5" wingspan allows him to challenge taller opponents, protect the rim, and finish above defenders around the basket. His offensive contributions remain largely restricted to putbacks and assisted finishes, while limited shooting range and average lateral mobility raise questions about his positional versatility.

23.name: Matt Brinkman
23.about: A polished senior wing, Brinkman capped his Oregon career as one of the nation's most dependable perimeter shooters and secondary playmakers. His quick release, intelligent off-ball movement, and ability to deliver accurate passes against rotating defenses make him an appealing offensive role player. However, his below-average athleticism, limited wingspan, and difficulty containing quicker opponents raise concerns about his defensive fit and overall upside at the NBA level.
23.weakness_3: Minimal shot creation off the dribble

24.name: Kevin Chavez
24.about: A relentless two-way competitor, Chavez emerged as Virginia's defensive tone-setter during his junior campaign, using his powerful frame, explosive lateral quickness, and 6'11" wingspan to overwhelm opposing perimeter players. His aggressive drives and transition finishing provided valuable offense, while his physicality made him a difficult matchup on both ends. Despite his defensive upside, inconsistent outside shooting and limited offensive creativity could restrict his role at the next level.
24.weakness_3: Undersized for a traditional small forward

25.name: Quinell Jones III
25.about: A rugged interior presence, Jones established himself as one of the ACC's most physical rebounders during his junior campaign at Boston College. His 248-pound frame, relentless pursuit of second-chance opportunities, and ability to finish through contact made him a dependable frontcourt contributor. While he occasionally flashed touch away from the basket, limited explosiveness, average defensive mobility, and an underdeveloped perimeter game raise concerns about his effectiveness against NBA frontcourts.

26.name: Ivan Zovko
26.about: Playing for Dubrava, Croatian prospect Ivan Zovko has attracted NBA interest through his creative interior scoring and developing face-up game. At 7'0" with a 7'5" wingspan, the left-handed big uses soft touch, clever footwork, and patient fakes to generate looks around the paint. His developing midrange jumper adds versatility, while his length gives him defensive upside. With continued physical development, Zovko could grow into a skilled rotation big who creates mismatches inside.

27.name: Amaziah Madaki
27.about: After transferring from Boston College, Madaki emerged as a physical defensive anchor and one of the Big Ten's most dependable rebounders during his junior season at Wisconsin. The Nigerian big man uses his 7'3" wingspan, powerful frame, and strong positioning to control the glass and protect the paint despite standing just 6'8". However, his extremely limited offensive range and inconsistent lateral mobility remain concerns entering the NBA.

28.name: Isaiah Nesbitt
28.about: A former Kentucky recruit who eventually found his footing at Creighton, Nesbitt developed into one of the Big East's most reliable perimeter scorers during his junior campaign. The 6'8" wing showcased smooth shooting mechanics, intelligent off-ball movement, and an ability to punish aggressive closeouts. Despite his offensive polish and positional size, limited explosiveness, a slender frame, and inconsistent defensive positioning remain concerns entering the NBA.

29.name: Taylen Henderson
29.about: A disruptive defensive presence, Henderson quickly established himself as one of Texas A&M's most versatile defenders during his freshman campaign. His 7'2" wingspan, impressive lateral quickness, and physical frame allow him to pressure ball handlers, disrupt passing lanes, and switch across multiple positions. Offensively, he showed encouraging catch-and-shoot ability and explosive finishing in transition, though limited self-creation and an inconsistent handle leave him projecting primarily as a complementary two-way forward.

30.name: Jordan-Élie Mbemba
30.about: A developing interior specialist, Mbemba earned a rotational role with Paris Basketball through his defensive activity, physical rebounding, and willingness to do the dirty work. The 6'9" French forward uses strong timing to challenge shots and create second-chance opportunities, providing valuable energy around the basket. However, his limited shooting range, inconsistent offensive touch, and lack of advanced ball skills leave him projecting as a defense-first frontcourt prospect with a relatively narrow offensive role.

31.name: Tre'Mont Willams
31.about: A powerful downhill scorer with impressive physical tools, Willams made his presence felt during his freshman season at Arizona. His explosive first step, muscular 218-pound frame and 6'11" wingspan allow him to overwhelm smaller defenders, absorb contact and finish emphatically around the rim. He also flashes intriguing defensive versatility, though his inconsistent perimeter jumper and limited playmaking currently prevent him from becoming a more complete offensive threat.

32.name: Izan Carrasco
32.about: An athletic Spanish forward with intriguing offensive versatility, Carrasco showcased explosive finishing and improved perimeter touch during his season with Valencia Basket. His mobility, quick first step, and ability to attack closeouts make him a dangerous cutter and transition finisher, while his developing jumper offers potential as a modern stretch forward. However, his slender frame, inconsistent defensive positioning, and limited physicality against stronger interior opponents remain concerns entering the NBA.

33.name: T.J. Ferrara
33.about: At Syracuse, T.J. Ferrara built a reputation as an energetic frontcourt finisher whose motor and athleticism consistently energized his team. The sophomore center thrives in transition, attacks the offensive glass, and finishes emphatically on lobs and dump-offs. His 7'3" wingspan gives him promising tools as a weak-side shot blocker, while his mobility suits modern pick-and-roll schemes. Ferrara's high-energy approach and developing interior defense provide a foundation for an NBA role as a rotation rim runner.

34.name: Damien Mitchell
34.about: A versatile senior forward, Mitchell emerged as the centerpiece of VCU's aggressive defensive identity while developing into a dependable offensive contributor. His combination of size, athleticism, and defensive instincts allowed him to guard multiple positions, while improved perimeter shooting complemented his powerful downhill attacks. Although his two-way versatility makes him an intriguing early-second-round prospect, inconsistent ball-handling and limited self-created offense raise questions about his long-term offensive ceiling.

35.name: Rashad McQueen
35.about: After transferring from Alabama, McQueen found his offensive rhythm at St. John's, developing into a dependable floor-spacing big during his junior campaign. His sturdy frame, confident perimeter jumper, and physical finishing allowed him to stretch opposing frontcourts while contributing as a screener and offensive rebounder. However, below-average athleticism, limited lateral quickness, and inconsistent rim protection raise concerns about his defensive fit against more mobile NBA forwards and centers.

36.name: Johnson Bloom
36.about: Bloom emerged as an intriguing developmental big during his freshman season at Texas, using his 6'10" frame and 7'3" wingspan to establish himself as a disruptive interior defender. His timing as a shot blocker, physical rebounding, and ability to finish above the rim give him a clear NBA role projection. However, his offensive game remains extremely limited outside the paint, while inconsistent defensive positioning and average lateral mobility restrict his versatility.

37.name: Austin Watson Jr
37.about: A polished perimeter scorer, Watson emerged as a dependable offensive weapon during his senior season at Georgia. His quick release, confident pull-up jumper and ability to navigate screens make him dangerous both on and off the ball. He can create his own looks when possessions break down, but average athleticism, limited defensive length and inconsistent playmaking restrict his upside as an NBA lead guard.

38.name: Kaspars Strautiņš
38.about: Strautiņš brings an intriguing combination of size, shooting touch and offensive versatility to the backcourt. The 6'6" Latvian has developed into a reliable perimeter threat against professional competition, showing the ability to knock down catch-and-shoot opportunities, relocate into open space and attack closeouts. His height gives him an advantage over smaller guards, but limited burst and inconsistent playmaking raise questions about his ability to create offense against NBA defenders.

39.name: Kellan Benjamin
39.about: Benjamin emerged as one of Utah's most versatile defensive weapons during his junior campaign, using exceptional mobility for his size to switch onto guards and contain drives along the perimeter. His 6'10" frame, quick feet, and active defensive instincts make him an intriguing modern frontcourt prospect. Offensively, he contributes through rim runs, cuts, and transition finishes, but inconsistent perimeter shooting and limited self-creation restrict his overall scoring ceiling.

40.name: Jared Jackson
40.about: Jackson carved out a valuable offensive role during his freshman season at Baylor, showcasing a polished perimeter jumper and impressive confidence shooting off screens. At 6'7" with a 6'11" wingspan, he possesses appealing size for an NBA floor spacer, particularly when operating away from the ball. However, his below-average athleticism, limited defensive mobility, and struggles creating separation against physical defenders leave him projecting as a specialized offensive contributor rather than a featured scorer.

41.name: Tyler Lamb
41.about: After transferring from Indiana to Santa Clara, Lamb enjoyed a breakout sophomore campaign, emerging as the Broncos' primary offensive weapon. The left-handed combo guard showcased his aggressive slashing ability, creative finishing and improved perimeter shooting while thriving in an expanded role. His scoring production has generated NBA interest, although his undersized frame, defensive limitations and developing playmaking skills remain concerns.

42.name: Quintin Allen
42.about: A physical, defense-first guard who established himself as one of Villanova's most reliable perimeter stoppers, Allen brings toughness, athleticism and relentless energy to both ends of the floor. Despite standing just 6'3", his strong frame and 6'9" wingspan allow him to defend bigger wings and disrupt opposing ball handlers. His offensive contributions come primarily through transition opportunities and aggressive drives, while inconsistent outside shooting and limited creation remain concerns.

43.name: Tyler Bloxam
43.about: After completing his senior season at UConn, Tyler Bloxam stood out as a dependable interior presence who brought energy, physicality, and defensive commitment to the frontcourt. At 6'11" with a 7'5" wingspan, he excels as a screen setter, offensive rebounder, and close-range finisher. His ability to run the floor and challenge shots around the basket gives him a straightforward role at the next level, with his best opportunity coming as an undrafted candidate competing for a depth-center position.

44.name: Anthony Myles
44.about: At Washington, Anthony Myles developed into a towering interior presence, using his 7'6" wingspan and imposing frame to influence possessions around the basket. The center prospect specializes in paint defense, offensive rebounding, and finishing close to the rim, where his size creates difficult matchups. His understanding of positioning and willingness to do the physical work make him an intriguing developmental big who could earn opportunities through interior defense and reliable screening.

45.name: Tyler Lee
45.about: Showing encouraging flashes during his freshman season at Kansas, Tyler Lee established himself as an energetic big man with the physical tools to develop into an effective NBA rim runner. His 7'4" wingspan and explosive leaping ability make him a natural lob target, while his activity on the offensive glass creates extra possessions. Lee runs the floor hard, finishes decisively around the basket, and has the athletic foundation to become a useful rotation center with continued development.

46.name: Malik Tanner
46.about: A powerful, explosive forward, Tanner concluded his North Carolina career as an energetic interior finisher and versatile defensive presence. His combination of strength, vertical athleticism, and a 7'0" wingspan allows him to attack the rim, finish through contact, and defend multiple positions. Despite his physical tools and experience, an unreliable perimeter jumper, limited offensive creativity, and inconsistent decision-making leave him projecting as an energy-oriented rotation player rather than a dependable scoring option.

47.name: Johnnie Sheffield
47.about: Sheffield carved out a valuable role at Maryland during his sophomore campaign, using his open-floor speed, athleticism, and defensive activity to generate transition opportunities. The 6'8" forward excels at pushing the ball after rebounds, finishing above the rim, and finding teammates on the break. However, his inconsistent perimeter jumper, limited half-court shot creation, and occasional lapses in defensive positioning leave him projecting as a developmental second-round prospect.

48.name: Basim James
48.about: A physical, experienced scorer, James finished his Illinois career as a dependable offensive option who used his strength to create space and punish smaller defenders. His sturdy frame, controlled pull-up jumper, and ability to absorb contact made him effective in the midrange and around the basket. However, his undersized profile for a forward, average explosiveness, and limited defensive versatility create questions about how consistently his scoring approach will translate to the NBA.

49.name: Jaylin Worthy
49.about: A skilled left-handed forward, Worthy concluded his Western Kentucky career as a dependable offensive contributor, using crafty footwork, soft shooting touch, and intelligent positioning to compensate for limited athleticism. His ability to stretch defenses, operate from the elbows, and make timely passes provides intriguing offensive versatility. However, his undersized frame for a frontcourt player, below-average lateral mobility, and inconsistent rim protection raise concerns about his defensive viability at the NBA level.

50.name: Ahmad McDaniels
50.about: During his freshman season at UCLA, Ahmad McDaniels brought a physical, hard-working presence to the frontcourt, establishing himself as an interior prospect who thrives on contact and effort plays. He finishes decisively around the basket, sets forceful screens, and competes for rebounds on both ends. His 7'3" wingspan offers useful defensive potential, while his strength and willingness to do the dirty work give him a pathway toward a developmental NBA role as an energy big.

51.name: Bacho Chikovani
51.about: Chikovani emerged as an intriguing developmental forward in Georgia's professional league, showcasing a physical offensive approach and promising passing instincts for his size. The 6'8" Georgian uses his sturdy frame to finish through contact, operate from the high post, and find cutters against rotating defenses. Although his versatility offers second-round appeal, inconsistent perimeter shooting, limited lateral quickness, and questions about his production against stronger competition remain significant concerns.

52.name: Liddell Jefferson Jr.
52.about: A versatile veteran guard, Jefferson provided Kentucky with dependable two-way production throughout his senior campaign. His combination of slashing instincts, reliable perimeter shooting and a 6'9" wingspan allows him to contribute without dominating the ball. He attacks closeouts effectively, competes defensively and offers secondary playmaking, though average athleticism and limited shot creation leave him projecting as a complementary NBA guard.

53.name: Terrence Smith
53.about: A dependable two-way contributor throughout his junior campaign at Wisconsin, Smith has developed into an intriguing second-round prospect thanks to his perimeter shooting and disciplined defensive approach. His 6'10" wingspan allows him to contest shots and defend multiple backcourt positions, while his reliable catch-and-shoot jumper makes him a valuable complementary offensive piece. Limited athleticism and an inability to consistently create his own offense raise questions about his NBA ceiling.

54.name: Tyquan Majors
54.about: Majors developed into a disruptive two-way guard at USC, combining advanced ball-handling skills with aggressive point-of-attack defense. Despite standing just 6'1", his impressive 6'7" wingspan allows him to pressure opposing ball handlers, disrupt passing lanes and compensate for his lack of height. Offensively, he uses a tight handle and deceptive changes of pace to create opportunities, though inconsistent shooting and limited explosiveness restrict his scoring ceiling.

55.name: Issa M'Bemba
55.about: An explosive young French guard with intriguing physical tools, M'Bemba has attracted NBA attention through his flashes of athleticism and defensive potential with Limoges CSP. His exceptional wingspan, quick first step and ability to finish above the rim make him dangerous in transition and attacking closeouts. However, inconsistent shooting, raw decision-making and a limited offensive role against professional competition leave him as a developmental second-round prospect.

56.name: Slobodan Krstić
56.about: With Partizan, Serbian big man Slobodan Krstić has developed an unconventional offensive game, using crafty footwork, touch, and surprising ball-handling ability to create scoring opportunities near the basket. Despite standing 6'9", he plays with the instincts of a skilled interior facilitator, finding cutters and keeping possessions alive with smart decisions. His strength and creative finishing give him a distinctive profile, while his professional experience provides a valuable foundation as he pursues a potential NBA opportunity.

57.name: Jean Giraud
57.about: Giraud is an intriguing young French guard whose speed, length and attacking instincts give him considerable developmental appeal. Despite his slender frame, he aggressively attacks open lanes, finishes creatively above the rim and uses his 6'10" wingspan to disrupt opposing ball handlers. His offensive production remains inconsistent against professional competition, while his perimeter jumper, physical strength and half-court decision-making require further refinement.

58.name: Daouda Sylla
58.about: Defensive disruption is Sylla's calling card, with his exceptional 6'11" wingspan allowing him to pressure ball handlers, jump passing lanes and contest shots well beyond his height. The Senegalese guard also contributes as a downhill attacker, using his length to finish around defenders in transition. His limited shooting range and raw offensive decision-making remain significant obstacles, but his defensive upside offers a potential NBA pathway.

59.name: Jaylen Woodard
59.about: Woodard concluded his Arizona career as a dependable interior contributor, relying on polished post footwork, soft touch around the basket, and strong positioning rather than athleticism. The 6'9" senior proved effective scoring through contact and securing defensive rebounds, but struggled to extend his offense beyond the paint. His limited explosiveness, lack of perimeter shooting, and defensive mobility concerns leave him projected as a fringe second-round prospect with a narrow NBA role.

60.name: Jonas Schweizer
60.about: A technically polished German wing, Schweizer carved out an important role at Duke through his perimeter shooting, disciplined defense and ability to create separation in the half court. The junior possesses a smooth shooting stroke, excellent footwork and the confidence to knock down difficult jumpers off the dribble. However, his below-average athleticism, limited explosiveness and struggles finishing against longer defenders raise questions about his ability to translate his scoring arsenal to the NBA.

61.name: Devon Rose
61.about: Rose flashed intriguing athletic tools during his sophomore season at Rutgers, using his length and open-floor speed to finish above the rim and contribute defensively. The 6'8" forward showed occasional promise as a spot-up shooter and weak-side cutter, but struggled to establish consistent offensive production. His slender frame, limited ball-handling, and inconsistent defensive awareness leave him projected as a likely undrafted prospect who could benefit from further development.

62.name: Dylan Swartz
62.about: Swartz emerged as one of the Ivy League's most productive perimeter scorers during his junior campaign at Yale, relying on polished shooting mechanics, intelligent off-ball movement and a deep offensive arsenal. The left-handed guard excels at navigating screens and knocking down difficult jumpers, making him an intriguing late-second-round prospect. However, his limited athleticism, short wingspan and defensive shortcomings present significant concerns about his ability to compete against NBA-caliber guards.

63.name: Jeremiah Wong
63.about: A mobile frontcourt prospect at BYU, Jeremiah Wong brings movement and finishing instincts that fit modern offensive systems. At 6'10" with a 7'2" wingspan, he runs the floor well, finds openings along the baseline, and converts scoring chances around the rim. His developing outside shot adds another dimension to his game, while his mobility and willingness to work away from the ball give him a promising foundation as a versatile rotation big.

64.name: Eli Parks
64.about: Parks established himself as a dependable perimeter scoring threat during his sophomore season at Colorado State, using polished footwork, a quick release and confident pull-up shooting to generate offense. He excels at finding space around ball screens and relocating for open threes, but his undersized frame and poor athleticism create significant defensive concerns. His NBA prospects largely depend on his ability to provide efficient shooting in a limited role.

65.name: Mateja Savić
65.about: A skilled Serbian floor general, Savić has shown flashes of intriguing offensive creativity against professional competition with Borac Čačak. His left-handed jumper, patient pick-and-roll approach and ability to find teammates give him a solid foundation as a developmental combo guard. However, limited explosiveness, inconsistent scoring efficiency and difficulty containing quicker opponents leave significant questions about his NBA readiness.

66.name: Kofi Sadeeki
66.about: At FIU, Ghanaian big man Kofi Sadeeki established himself as a physical frontcourt presence who brings toughness, rebounding, and interior finishing. His 7'5" wingspan helps him contest shots and secure space around the basket, while his left-handed touch gives him a distinctive finishing style in traffic. Sadeeki embraces the demanding work of the center position, setting solid screens, battling for rebounds, and providing an energetic interior presence with potential to earn a role as a defensive-minded rotation big.

67.name: Sam Beasley
67.about: A seasoned scoring wing who became a focal point of Tulane's offense, Beasley enters the draft following a productive senior campaign built around his perimeter shot-making and offensive experience. He excels at finding space along the three-point line, attacking closeouts and converting difficult jumpers when possessions break down. Despite his scoring instincts, average positional size, limited explosiveness and defensive inconsistencies leave him fighting for consideration near the end of the draft.

68.name: K'eon Adams
68.about: An unusually tall shooting guard with intriguing offensive versatility, Adams finished his senior season at South Florida as a dangerous perimeter scorer capable of creating his own shot. His 6'8" frame, fluid ball handling and smooth shooting stroke allow him to rise over smaller defenders and generate offense from the wings. Despite his appealing combination of size and skill, a slender frame, inconsistent defensive physicality and questionable shot selection have kept him on the fringes of draft consideration.

69.name: Endre Baranyai
69.about: A skilled but athletically limited forward, Baranyai spent his season with Alba Fehérvár showcasing soft midrange touch, patient footwork, and an understanding of offensive spacing. The Hungarian prospect uses his sturdy frame to establish position and finish through contact, though his production remained modest against professional competition. Below-average explosiveness, limited defensive versatility, and an inconsistent outside jumper leave him projected as a likely undrafted prospect.

70.name: Danylo Yaremchuk
70.about: Yaremchuk spent his season with ALBA Berlin providing occasional scoring and secondary playmaking in a limited professional role. The 21-year-old Ukrainian wing possesses a sturdy frame, soft shooting touch, and a crafty turnaround jumper that allows him to create separation without elite athleticism. However, inconsistent efficiency, limited defensive quickness, and difficulty generating offense against higher-level defenders leave him projected as a likely undrafted prospect with potential overseas staying power.

71.name: Isaias Roman
71.about: Roman established himself as a physical interior presence during his junior season at New Mexico State, using his 238-pound frame to battle for rebounds and generate second-chance opportunities. His strength, positioning, and ability to finish through contact made him a reliable contributor around the basket. However, his lack of explosiveness, limited offensive range, and struggles defending quicker opponents leave him projected as an undrafted prospect who could compete for a developmental opportunity.

72.name: Andy Tavares
72.about: A veteran combo guard who provided Florida with steady offensive leadership throughout his senior campaign, Tavares combines confident perimeter shooting with crafty ball handling and solid playmaking instincts. He excels at operating pick-and-roll sets, creating opportunities for teammates and knocking down pull-up jumpers when defenders go under screens. However, his undersized frame, limited wingspan and relatively modest athletic upside make him a likely undrafted prospect despite his productive collegiate career.

73.name: Ang Jung Kai
73.about: Virginia's frontcourt gains extraordinary size from Singaporean center Ang Jung Kai, who stands 7'4" with an imposing 7'9" wingspan and a powerful 290-pound frame. He uses his physical presence to occupy space in the paint, battle for rebounds, and establish deep post position. His patient approach around the basket and willingness to embrace a traditional center role give him a distinctive profile, with opportunities to contribute through screening, interior finishing, and sheer size at the next level.

74.name: Nick Jacobson
74.about: A polished perimeter shot and versatile offensive approach helped Nick Jacobson finish his senior career at Central Michigan as an undersized frontcourt player with a potential professional role. His 75-rated three-point shooting gives him the ability to stretch the floor, while his left-handed release and willingness to take open jumpers make him a useful spacing option. Jacobson's experience, shooting touch, and flexibility between power forward and center give him a potential pathway into a professional rotation.

75.name: Zédarius Butler
75.about: A veteran defensive specialist, Butler concluded his Michigan State career as a physical, energetic forward who made his greatest impact through hustle plays, transition finishing, and defensive versatility. His 7'0" wingspan and solid athleticism allowed him to challenge shots and guard multiple positions. However, at 24 years old, his inconsistent perimeter shooting, limited offensive creation, and modest production leave him firmly in undrafted territory despite his useful defensive tools.
